statements.subject: message
statements.description: All transport-related parameters SHALL be included in the Transport header; the use of other headers for this purpose is NOT RECOMMENDED due to middleboxes, such as firewalls or NATs.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: All transport-related parameters SHALL be included in the Transport header; the use of other headers for this purpose is NOT RECOMMENDED due to middleboxes, such as firewalls or NATs.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For the benefit of any intervening firewalls, a client MUST indicate the known transport parameters, even if it has no influence over these parameters, for example, where the server advertises a fixed-multicast address as destination.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST include the Accept-Ranges header in the request, indicating all supported unit formats in the Range header.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client does not support a time format necessary for the presentation, the server MUST respond using 456 (Header Field Not Valid for Resource) and include the Accept-Ranges header with the range unit formats supported for the resource.
actions: include Accept-Ranges header with supported range unit formats

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In a SETUP response, the server MUST include the Accept-Ranges header (see Section 18.5) to indicate which time formats are acceptable to use for this media resource.
actions: include Accept-Ranges header in SETUP response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The SETUP 200 OK response MUST include the Media-Properties header (see Section 18.29).
actions: include Media-Properties header in SETUP 200 OK response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The SETUP 200 OK response MUST include the Media-Range header (see Section 18.30) if the media is Time-Progressing.
actions: include Media-Range header in SETUP 200 OK response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST generate a session identifier in response to a successful SETUP request unless a SETUP request to a server includes a session identifier or a Pipelined-Requests header referencing an existing session context.
actions: include Session header with session identifier in SETUP response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In that latter case, the server MUST bundle this SETUP request into the existing session (aggregated session) or return a 459 (Aggregate Operation Not Allowed) error code (see Section 17.4.23).
actions: bundle SETUP request into existing session
or return 459 Aggregate Operation Not Allowed error

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An aggregate control URI MUST be used to control an aggregated session.
actions: use aggregate control URI for session control requests

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This URI MUST be different from the stream control URIs of the individual media streams included in the aggregate (see Section 13.4.2 for aggregated sessions and for the particular URIs see Appendix D.1.1).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: However, even if aggregated control is offered, the client MAY choose not to set up the session in aggregated control.
actions: set up session without aggregated control

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY remove a session that has not demonstrated liveness signs from the client(s) within a certain timeout period.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The default timeout value is 60 seconds; the server MAY set this to a different value and indicate so in the timeout field of the Session header in the SETUP response.
actions: set session timeout to non-default value
include timeout field in Session header of SETUP response

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a SETUP request on a session fails for any reason, the session state, as well as transport and other parameters for associated streams, MUST remain unchanged from their values as if the SETUP request had never been received by the server.
actions: preserve transport parameters for associated streams unchanged
